cues: You can see this law everywhere.
A diver tucks in tight to somersault quickly, then stretches out to slow the spin before entering the water.
A planet moves faster when it is closer to the Sun, because gravity pulls straight towards the Sun and exerts no torque.
And a spinning top resists falling over, because tipping it would change the direction of its angular momentum.
text: You can see this law everywhere. A diver tucks in tight to somersault quickly, then stretches out to slow the spin before entering the water. A planet moves faster when it is closer to the Sun, because gravity pulls straight towards the Sun and exerts no torque. That is Kepler's second law. And a spinning top resists falling over, because tipping it would change the direction of its angular momentum.
